title: 2. ‘在那个时代’：宗教符号的双重性
originalTitle: 2. ‘In illo tempore’: The Ambivalence of Religious Symbols

children: 2. ‘In illo tempore’: The Ambivalence of Religious Symbols

zh: 2. ‘在那个时代’：宗教符号的双重性

en: Usually the materialist prefers to give meta-history a wide berth. But in doing so she renounces in advance her most ambitious and delicate task: grasping the
aspect of meta-history itself, the changing forms in which it emerges practically in the course of time: in sum, its
destiny. And she risks also giving a wide berth to an adequate understanding of capitalism.
zh: 唯物主义者通常宁愿远远避开元历史。但这样做时，她预先放弃了自己最有雄心、也最微妙的任务：把握元历史自身的物质方面，把握它在时间进程中实际显现的变化形式——总之，把握它的历史命运。她还有可能同时避开对资本主义的充分理解。

en: In pre-capitalist societies, meta-history had an external, concrete expression in religious worship. We should at
once note a difference of great significance. While capitalism
meta-history into social and economic history, not leaving any residues and to the point of making the two planes indistinguishable, religion

meta-history to historical facts, assigning it a special, separate sphere: the sacred time in which becoming is suspended or negated. And yet the full integration of history and meta-history can only be wholly deciphered in light of their prior counterposition. The true precursor of the capitalist mode of production is not so much another mode of production (serf labour on feudal estates, for example), as the complex of beliefs, mythical-ritual symbols and collective practices that go under the name ‘religion’. Historical materialism sometimes falls short of its principle discovery, the concept of labour-power, because it is almost never materialist enough to understand the significance of religious experience in all its depth.
zh: 在前资本主义社会中，元历史在宗教礼拜中获得一种外在的具体表达。我们应当立即注意一个意义重大的差异。资本主义把元历史纳入社会经济史，不留下任何残余，甚至使两个平面变得不可区分；宗教却把元历史同历史事实对置，给它划出一个特殊而分离的领域：生成在其中被悬置或否定的神圣时间。然而，只有借助历史与元历史此前的对置，二者的充分整合才可能得到彻底解读。资本主义生产方式真正的先驱，与其说是另一种生产方式——例如封建庄园中的农奴劳动——不如说是以‘宗教’之名统称的信仰、神话—仪式符号和集体实践的复合体。历史唯物主义有时没有达到它的首要发现——劳动力概念——的高度，是因为它几乎从来不够唯物主义，无法充分深入地理解宗教经验的意义。

en: Sacred time is a representation of the
and

of historical time: and for this reason it goes beyond and lies outside it. And only for this reason, note. The representation of that which has made history possible does not sit within the usual catalogue of historical events, but refers, instead, to an ‘other-then’ which is the substratum of chronology. The origin of the cosmos, of life, of becoming, is situated in an indefinite past:

. Liturgy connects the actual situation to the absolute beginning of all things. Ernesto de Martino writes that ‘Ritual is the behaviour that refers the historical “this time” ever back to the meta-historical “one time”, which is also a “once and for all time”.’
The

endeavour which is now underway draws legitimacy and value from its enduring, intimate link to a mythical not-now, a prior state to which is attributed the invariance of an archetype. According to Mircea Eliade, ‘the act takes on meaning and reality only to the extent that it reprises a primordial activity’.
It draws meaning, that is, if it renounces any contingent singularity of its own and shows that it is a
zh: 神圣时间是对历史时间之发生和基础的表象；正因如此，它超越历史时间并置身其外——请注意，也只是出于这个理由。对使历史成为可能之物的表象，并不处在通常的历史事件目录之中，而是指向一个作为年代基底的‘另一个那时’。宇宙、生命和生成的起源被安置在一个不确定过去：in illo tempore，即‘在那个时代’。礼仪把现实处境同万物的绝对开端联结起来。埃内斯托·德·马蒂诺写道：‘仪式是一种行为，它不断把历史的“这一次”回指元历史的“某一次”，而后者同时也是“一次而永远”。’
眼下正在进行的努力，从它同神话性非现在、同一个被赋予原型不变性的先前状态之间持久而紧密的联系中，取得正当性与价值。依照米尔恰·伊利亚德的说法，‘一项行动只有在重演一项原初活动的范围内，才取得意义与现实性’。
也就是说，只有放弃自身任何偶然的独特性，并表明自己是一场重复演出，它才取得意义。

en: The relation between the historical ‘this time’ and the meta-historical ‘once and for all’ is a representation of the relation between act and potential. The origin is chaos, still-indeterminate
, in the mythical epoch, everything was possible. Then, types were not fixed and forms remained fluid … Moreover, fluidity of forms was also a symptom of the
at the other extremity of time, from the moment in which history ended and the whole world began to live in a sacred time, in eternity.’
But the image of

as fluctuating potentiality does not provide any basis for the present activity. Chaos is inimitable. For this reason, in religious worship, potential is supplanted by a surreptitious and yet useable double: the
, the progenitor of a series (the first hunt, the first sacrifice, the first sexual coupling, realised
by demi-gods or heroes).

, which remains the same as it relates to each single act, takes on the misleading guise of an immutable, ancestral act; it becomes a normative model, which must be ritually repeated in order to avoid the uncertainty and dangers that attend the historical ‘this time’. The

reduction of potential to a repeatable prototype is the cornerstone of those doctrines that postulate the cyclical nature of time (the eternal return of the same thing, the periodic regeneration of the cosmos, etc.).
zh: 历史的‘这一次’与元历史的‘一次而永远’之间的关系，是实现与潜能关系的表象。起源是混沌，是仍未确定的 dynamis：‘在那个时代，在神话时代，一切皆有可能。那时，类型尚未固定，形式仍在流动……此外，形式的流动性也是时间另一端之末世的征兆；从历史终结、整个世界开始生活在神圣时间和永恒中的那个时刻起便是如此。’

但把 illud tempus——‘那个时间’——描绘成流动潜在性的影像，不能为当下活动提供任何根据。混沌无法模仿。因此，在宗教礼拜中，潜能被一个暗中替换却可供使用的复本取代：开创性行动，即一个系列的始祖——第一次狩猎、第一次献祭、第一次性交，由半神或英雄在 in illo tempore 完成。同每项单一实现发生关系时始终保持相同的 dynamis，披上了不变祖传行动这一误导性外衣；它成为必须在仪式中重复的规范模型，以避免伴随历史‘这一次’的不确定性与危险。把潜能还原为可重复原型，是那些设定时间具有循环性质之教义的基石——同一事物的永恒复归、宇宙的周期性再生等等。

en: The mystical-ritual representation of the
and

of history is directed against history itself, against the proliferation or metastasis of its concrete contents. And this is the decisive point: the liturgical image that refutes or paralyses becoming is the very thing that allows for it. The repetition of the archetype, of an inaugural act accomplished

, interrupts the succession of chronology: a series of unique (historical) events is replaced with a reversible series of identical events (copies conforming to the meta-historical model). Eliade: ‘time is abolished through the imitation of archetypes and the repetition of paradigmatic acts’.
De Martino:
zh: 对历史之发生和基础的神秘—仪式表象，针对历史本身，针对历史具体内容的增殖或扩散。而决定性的要点是：否定或瘫痪生成的礼仪影像，恰恰也是使生成成为可能的东西。重复在 in illo tempore 完成的原型或开创性行动，会中断年代的接续：一系列独一无二的历史事件，被一系列可逆的同一事件——符合元历史模型的复制品——取代。伊利亚德说：‘通过模仿原型和重复范例性行动，时间被废除。’
德·马蒂诺：

en: The dehistoricisation of a critical moment of existence is, first of all, the ‘myth’ of that moment. Secondly, it is the possibility of repeating this myth every time that this determinate moment presents itself; that is, ‘ritual’. An organic system of mythical-ritual dehistoricisations, comprising the critical recurrent moments of a certain regime of existence, forms a religion.
zh: 首先，一个生存危机时刻的去历史化，就是这个时刻的‘神话’。其次，每当这个确定时刻出现，都存在重复这一神话的可能性；这就是‘仪式’。一个由神话—仪式性去历史化构成的有机体系，包含某种生存体制反复出现的危机时刻，它便形成一种宗教。

en: Gerard van der Leeuw speaks of ‘Birth, Marriage, and Death: Life as it directs itself to Power and is seized upon by Power; therefore not the personal life of feeling, not

the life of thought, but simply Life in its stark nakedness … Actually, even birth, marriage and death are still too ample. Birth and death suffice … As over against Power there is no history, neither collective nor individual.’

Which is to say: the life of which van der Leeuw speaks, dehistoricised because it is invested with sacred potential, is wholly analogous to the ‘immediate bodily existence’ which under capitalism functions as the characteristic or substratum of labour-power (potential turned into a commodity).
zh: 赫拉德·范德莱乌谈到‘出生、婚姻与死亡：生命朝向力量而行，并被力量攫取；因此，不是个人的感情生活，不是思想生活，而只是赤裸裸的生命……事实上，即使出生、婚姻和死亡也仍然过于宽泛。出生与死亡就已足够……面对力量，不存在历史，既无集体历史，也无个体历史。’
也就是说，范德莱乌所说的生命，因为被赋予神圣潜能而去历史化，它完全类似资本主义下作为劳动力——变成商品的潜能——之特征或基底发挥作用的‘直接身体存在’。

en: The clash between Eliade’s and de Martino’s ways of understanding the religious impulse to abrogate history is of great interest. For Eliade, the irreversibility of becoming is a ‘secondary’ – indeed, pathological – characteristic of experience; its primary – constant and unavoidable – characteristic is its negation. The sacred is a direct expression of this anti-historical impulse, this vocation to see off the pestering of the ‘ever new’.

The sacred is primary, then: it does not submit to explanation on the basis of extrinsic elements (and still less on the basis of the same historical vicissitudes that it itself suspends and emasculates). De Martino objects: ‘Eliade says that man is opposed to history even when he claims to be nothing
but history. But note, we could also say the opposite, that man is part of history even when he claims to go beyond it with his mythical-ritual behaviour.’

Eliade stops short in deference to the meta-historical character of religion, holding it to be unquestionable. De Martino, conversely, proposes to demonstrate the genuinely historical reality and significance of meta-history; or better still, the nature of its unexpected
function. Crude materialism is closer to Eliade than to de Martino. Indeed, Eliade, too, sees in religious worship

an escape from history. It is a justifiable, genuine escape, in Eliade’s view – a pusillanimous, illusory one in the view of our perfunctory materialists. But what is the difference? In both cases, practice is stashed in the archives, ruling that there are no grounds to proceed. In both cases, the salient question is left unaddressed. The mythical-ritual symbols responsible for the re-evocation of origin and archetypes represent the conditions of possibility of concrete historical praxis. As such, these symbols are always correlated to this praxis, even though opposed to it; indeed, they are at its very centre. Thus their opposition emerges on account of their excessive proximity, and not from an insurmountable separation. And it does not seem plausible that we are here dealing
with an opposition.
zh: 伊利亚德与德·马蒂诺理解宗教废除历史之冲动的方式彼此冲突，这一点极富意义。对伊利亚德而言，生成的不可逆性是经验的‘次要’——实际上是病理性——特征；经验首要、恒常且不可避免的特征，反而是对这种不可逆性的否定。神圣是这种反历史冲动、这种摆脱‘永远新异者’之纠缠的天职的直接表达。
因而神圣具有首要地位：不能用外在要素解释它，更不能用它自身所悬置和阉割的那些历史变迁来解释。德·马蒂诺反驳说：‘伊利亚德说，即使人声称自己无非就是历史，人仍反对历史。但请注意，我们也可以反过来说，即使人声称以神话—仪式行为超越历史，他仍然是历史的一部分。’

伊利亚德出于对宗教元历史性质的敬畏止步于此，把这种性质视为不容质疑。相反，德·马蒂诺主张展示元历史真正的历史现实与意义；更准确地说，展示它那出人意料的历史化功能。粗陋唯物主义更接近伊利亚德，而非德·马蒂诺。事实上，伊利亚德同样只在宗教礼拜中看见对历史的逃离；在伊利亚德看来，这种逃离正当且真实，在我们草率的唯物主义者看来则怯懦而虚幻。但二者究竟有什么区别？两种情形都把问题草草归档，仿佛已裁定没有继续追究的理由；两种情形都没有触及突出的关键问题。负责重现起源与原型的神话—仪式符号，代表具体历史实践的可能性条件。作为这种条件，这些符号即使同实践对立，也始终同它相关；事实上，它们正处在实践的中心。因此，它们的对立源自过度接近，而非不可跨越的分离。而且，我们在这里面对的似乎不可能仅仅是对立。

en: It was de Martino (and not Löwith, Taubes, or anyone else) who delineated a radically new situation in terms of the thinking on historical time. However, for our purposes it suffices to make a summary reference to a thesis that frequently recurred throughout his works. For de Martino, mystical-ritual meta-history is
: that is, it fulfils two roles which seem mutually contradictory.

If on the one hand it dehistoricises, offering protection from ‘the uncontrolled proliferation of becoming’, on the other it nonetheless provides a ‘means of reprising and redeeming historical experience’.

The liturgy veils the variety of contingent actions that follow one another in time, reducing them to certain immutable archetypes; yet precisely for this reason, it allows for a trauma-free multiplication of these same actions. ‘All religions are born of that experience of the present which does not hold firm in the face of history (anguishes over history), and they constitute a means of

children: opening the way to history through the mediation of dehistoricisation

en: : religions are systems of dehistoricising the critical moments of existence, such that presence might emerge from them unscathed.’
The ritual interruption of chronological progression affords the opportunity to ‘stand within history
we were not doing so’.
The escape-tunnel is also an access-route: in simulating stopping and retraction, we ready ourselves for a new beginning; the apotropaic ‘as if’ rekindles our ‘profane industry’ anew.
zh: 正是德·马蒂诺——不是勒维特、陶伯斯或其他人——在思考历史时间方面勾勒出一种全新处境。不过，就我们的目的而言，只需概括提及一个在他作品中反复出现的论题。对德·马蒂诺而言，神秘—仪式的元历史具有双重性：它履行两个看似彼此矛盾的角色。一方面，它实行去历史化，保护人免受‘生成失控的增殖’；另一方面，它又提供‘重新接续并救赎历史经验的手段’。
礼仪遮蔽时间中相继发生的多样偶然行动，把它们还原为某些不变原型；但恰恰因此，它使这些行动能够无创伤地增殖。‘所有宗教都诞生于当下面对历史无法站稳——因历史而焦虑——的经验；它们构成一种通过去历史化的中介打开通向历史之道路的手段：宗教是使生存危机时刻去历史化的体系，使在场得以毫发无伤地从中出现。’
仪式性中断年代推进，使人有机会‘仿佛并不身处历史那样身处历史’。
逃生隧道也是进入路径：通过模拟停顿与撤回，我们为新的开始做好准备；具有禳灾作用的‘仿佛’重新点燃我们的‘世俗劳作’。

en: It is worth adding a marginal commentary on de Martino’s analysis. The mythical-ritual symbol does not wholly coincide with the ambivalent role it plays. That is, it is insufficient to define it as the mechanism that discredits
rehabilitates historical experience in one fell swoop. This symbol is, first of all, an image of the
and
of history. Its ambivalence sinks its roots in this representative content. When history’s genesis and foundation are portrayed in religious worship, they seem

to reabsorb the multiple historical occurrences to which they have given rise; thus tending to kill their own offspring. On the other hand, the liturgical representation itself proves that the genesis and foundation are still at work, omnipresent and contiguous to each single action; there is no moment of chronological succession in which history is not restarting afresh.
zh: 值得对德·马蒂诺的分析补充一条旁注。神话—仪式符号并不完全等同于它所扮演的双重角色。也就是说，仅仅把它定义为一举贬低并恢复历史经验的机制并不充分。首先，这个符号是历史之发生和基础的影像；它的双重性扎根于这种表象内容。当历史的发生和基础在宗教礼拜中得到描绘时，它们似乎重新吸收自己所产生的多重历史事件，因而趋向杀死自己的后代。另一方面，礼仪表象本身证明，发生与基础仍然在起作用，无所不在并同每项单一行动接壤；在年代接续中，没有任何时刻不是历史重新开始的时刻。

en: The limitation of religious worship does not, of course, lie in its according considerable significance to meta-history, but in the fact that it accords it
. The defect of the mystical-symbolic ritual is not that it hopes to represent the presuppositions of historical praxis, but that it hopes

to represent them. Being itself encapsulated within historical time, meta-history does, indeed, achieve a sort of external existence, but it is a partial, circumscribed, extremely modest one. It would be a grave error to believe that capitalism is anti-religious because it rejects meta-history; on the contrary, it is anti-religious because it extends meta-history far beyond the confines set down by liturgy, guaranteeing it the full brilliance that befits a productive force. Capitalism realises in practice that which de Martino himself poses as an object of study: namely, to
. It amalgamates and unites the two poles which religion separates out;

is no longer counterposed to becoming, but becomes an indelible component of it; shards of sacred time are sunk in every fold or interstice of historical time; meta-history, far from having to be evoked with reflected images, emerges at surface-level with the irrefutable evidence of concrete phenomena.
zh: 宗教礼拜的局限，当然不在于它赋予元历史相当大的意义，而在于赋予得太少。神秘—象征仪式的缺陷，并非它希望表象历史实践的诸前提，而是它只希望表象这些前提。元历史自身被包含于历史时间之中，确实取得某种外在存在，但这种存在局部、有限且极其微弱。如果以为资本主义反宗教是因为它拒绝元历史，那将是严重错误。相反，它反宗教，是因为它把元历史远远扩展到礼仪所划定的边界之外，保证元历史取得作为生产力所应有的全部光辉。资本主义在实践中实现德·马蒂诺本人设定为研究对象的事情：使元历史历史化。它混合并统一宗教所分离的两极；illud tempus 不再同生成对置，而成为生成不可磨灭的构件；神圣时间的碎片沉入历史时间的每一道褶皱或间隙；元历史不再必须借助反射影像得到唤起，而是带着具体现象无可辩驳的明证浮现于表面。

en: The capitalist mode of production is pervaded, from top to bottom, by the

typical of the mythical-ritual symbol. The oscillation between history stopping and its being unleashed in intensified form is not represented by some special aspect of worship, but rather takes root everywhere, characterising the entire organisation of society. Two antithetical states of mind alternate – or more often, accompany one another – each of them emitting its own organ-grinder’s tune. It is said that in capitalism, the pace of time is accelerated, all that is solid hurries to melt into air, and the only reasonable thing to expect is the surprise of the unpredictable. But it is also said that in capitalism time is turned to stone, the vortex of change cannot hide the monotonous repetition of unalterable archetypes, and that everyday surprises are trite and all too well known to us.
zh: 资本主义生产方式从上到下都被神话—仪式符号特有的双重性贯穿。历史停止与历史以强化形式释放之间的摆动，不再由某个特定的礼拜环节来表象，而是在各处扎根，刻画整个社会组织。两种对立心态交替出现——更常见的是彼此相伴——各自奏响自己的街头风琴曲。有人说，在资本主义中，时间步伐加快，一切坚固的东西都匆忙消散在空气中，唯一合理的期待就是不可预测者带来的惊奇。但也有人说，在资本主义中，时间化为石头，变化的漩涡无法掩盖不变原型的单调重复，而日常惊奇陈腐不堪，早已为我们所熟知。

en: The ambivalence no longer appears in a symbolic representation, but in the material reality of labour-power. We know that the faculty for production, ‘labour as subjectivity’, lends itself to a dual interpretation: as a category
peculiar to capitalist society, and as an anthropological requisite inherent within any epoch. The whole difficulty lies in understanding that capitalism is an absolutely
socio-economic formation precisely because it gives the most
anthropological requisites an empirical appearance; because it makes potential as such into a use-value that can be alienated in exchange for money. Labour-power, by itself, nonetheless produces a

effect: it seems to be a considerable ‘historic result’ but also the ‘point of departure of history’; something unprecedented, but also an archetype that is valid for all time. Meta-history is materialised in a historically definite situation: yet this true-enough statement is never immune to the risk of being turned upside-down by the loose talk that provides its mirror-image, according to which it is instead history that breaks up into an ensemble of meta-historical relations.
zh: 双重性不再出现于象征表象，而是出现于劳动力的物质现实。我们知道，生产官能即‘作为主体性的劳动’，可以得到双重解释：既是资本主义社会特有的范畴，也是任何时代都内在具有的人类学条件。全部困难都在于理解：资本主义之所以是一种绝对特殊的社会经济形态，恰恰是因为它赋予最一般的人类学条件以经验外观；因为它使潜能本身成为能够让渡以换取货币的使用价值。然而劳动力本身会产生一种错视效果（trompe-l’œil）：它似乎既是重大的‘历史结果’，又是‘历史的出发点’；既是前所未有之物，又是对所有时间都有效的原型。元历史在一种历史上确定的处境中物质化；然而，这个完全正确的陈述从来不能免除被其镜像式空谈颠倒的风险——依照后者，反而是历史分解成了一组元历史关系。

en: In passing from the mythical-ritual symbol to the buying and selling of labour-power, the ambivalence changes in both appearance and function. Religion
and suspends history through the liturgical representation of its origin: but, in so doing, makes it bearable and allows for its resumption. On the contrary, capitalism

the historicity of experience in clear figures, on the terrain of phenomena; but, in so doing, it seems to exhaust this historicity once and for all time. Dehistoricisation is not some middle stage, but its end result. The ambivalence is no longer a therapeutic parenthesis, but the
(and pathological) consequence of a history so heavily populated that it can count among its immediate contents no less than the genesis and foundation of all historical praxis.
zh: 从神话—仪式符号转向劳动力买卖时，双重性的外观与功能都发生变化。宗教通过对历史起源的礼仪表象遮蔽并悬置历史；但这样做时，它又使历史变得可以承受，并使历史得以重新开始。相反，资本主义在现象层面以清晰形态展示经验的历史性；但这样做时，它又显得已经一劳永逸地穷尽这种历史性。去历史化不再是某个中间阶段，而成为最终结果。双重性不再是一段治疗性的插曲，而是一种内容如此稠密之历史的永久且病理性的后果；因为这种历史甚至把一切历史实践的发生与基础算入自己的直接内容。

en: In capitalism, we cannot ‘stand within history
we
were not doing so’. For one clear reason: meta-history, which had previously provided us with an escape-tunnel (the

) is now an integral part of that history which we were hypothetically meant to be escaping. What we can do, in recompense, is believe that the hustle and bustle of history has now come to an end, in its entirety. Capitalism understands itself to be the
, the conclusion, the end of time. But with one important qualification: it is not an
to be prefigured and awaited. The end has

crept up on us: without any clamour, and, above all, without any Judgment. As de Martino puts it: ‘We experience a fulfilled prophecy, rather than awaiting it. Contemporary apocalyptics (or eschatology) do not have to defend themselves on account of unrealised predictions, but rather have to manage living with their own success.’
zh: 在资本主义中，我们无法‘仿佛并不身处历史那样身处历史’。理由很清楚：此前为我们提供逃生隧道——那个‘仿佛’——的元历史，如今已经成为我们假想要逃离之历史的组成部分。作为补偿，我们能够相信，历史的全部喧嚣现在已经彻底终结。资本主义把自己理解成末世（eschaton）、结局、时间的终结。但有一项重要限定：它不是有待预示和等待的末世。终结已经悄悄降临到我们身边：没有任何喧闹，尤其没有任何审判。用德·马蒂诺的话说：‘我们经验一个已经实现的预言，而不是等待它。当代启示论——或末世论——无须因为预言尚未实现而为自身辩护，却必须设法同自身的成功共处。’

zh: 请考虑经济基础（structure）——生产关系——相对于上层建筑——法律、政治、宗教等等——的首要地位。很少有一个论题招致如此多的责难，而且理由非常充分。为它辩护的唯一方式是迂回且悖论式的。必须限制它的适用领域：只有在资本主义中，‘经济基础’才享有赤裸的优先地位。为什么？因为只有在资本主义中，生产关系本身才把元历史——使一般经验历史化的条件——算作自身的物质因素。然而，由此可以得出，只有最大限度地考虑‘上层建筑’中最飘忽的方面——即元历史长期借以得到表达的宗教传统——才能充分理解资本主义的‘经济基础’。马克思在《德意志意识形态》（第一部分B，marxists.org）中有一句评论；它虽然出于无可争辩的论战需要，单独来看却相当刺耳：‘法国人和英国人至少坚持政治幻想，这种幻想还多少接近现实；德国人却在“纯粹精神”的领域中活动，把宗教幻想变成历史的推动力。’所以，谈到成熟资本主义，我们反而应当说，更接近生产方式现实——接近‘经济基础’——的是宗教幻想，而不是政治幻想。
en: Consider the primacy of structure (the relations of production) over superstructure (law, politics, religion, etc.). Rarely has a thesis attracted such opprobrium – and for very good reasons. The only way to defend it is oblique and paradoxical. It is necessary to limit its field of application:
in capitalism does the economic ‘structure’ enjoy a bare pre-eminence. Why? Because

in capitalism does the production relation itself count meta-history (the requisites for historicising experience in general) among its material factors. From this it follows, however, that the capitalist ‘structure’ can be fully understood only with maximum consideration of the most ethereal aspect of ‘superstructure’: namely, the religious tradition within which meta-history has long found expression. In the
(Part 1, B, at

), Marx made a comment which, although resulting from incontestable polemical requirements, really jars when taken by itself: ‘While the French and the English at least hold by the political illusion, which is moderately close to reality, the Germans move in the realm of the “pure spirit”, and make religious illusion the driving force of history.’ So in reference to mature capitalism we ought to say, instead, that it is the religious illusion, and not the political one, that comes closer to the reality of the mode of production – to the ‘structure’.
